lead.headline: UN climate talks in Turkey collapse without a deal over fossil fuels
more: The EU, speaking through Irish minister Darragh O'Brien, called the omission of fossil fuels unconscionable. Panama called the text a rollback, the Marshall Islands said it had been let down on all sides, and Britain said the proposal moved backward on the science. Many delegations also objected to a carbon capture goal for industrial polluters, which critics said would undercut emissions cuts.

Chris Bowen, Australia's climate minister and COP31's president of negotiations, called the outcome very disappointing and said the 2023 Dubai agreement's call to transition away from fossil fuels remains in force. Palau, which backed the text despite its flaws, said other work programs were approved and the meeting was not a failure.
A separate pledge outside the main agreement, to raise electricity's share of final energy use from about 21 percent to 35 percent by 2035, drew nearly 100 signatories.
lead.summary: The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, ended Sunday without an overarching agreement after running nearly 48 hours past its scheduled close. The final proposal from the Turkish and Australian leadership left out any mention of fossil fuels, which the European Union and several other countries said they could not accept. Russia and Saudi Arabia had pushed to keep fossil fuels out of the text, while a larger group of nations reluctantly backed it to preserve consensus. Decisions on moving away from fossil fuels, adaptation money for poorer countries and gender and climate were pushed to next year's talks in Ethiopia.

briefs.text: A single player won Saturday's 47.14 million franc Swiss Lotto jackpot, the third-largest in the game's history, according to Swisslos.

stories.headline: Backlash grows over SVP's all-German-speaking ticket for Parmelin seat
more: Anger is strongest in French-speaking Switzerland, which has no candidate on the ticket. Jean-Luc Addor, head of the SVP's French-speaking group, called it an affront to the region, to women and to Geneva's Celine Amaudruz, who was eliminated in the caucus vote. According to SRF, Graber narrowly beat Bernese Jura cantonal minister Pierre Alain Schnegg after most of Amaudruz's supporters switched to him.

Any challenger would need far more than the left's votes: the Social Democrats, Greens and Green Liberals hold 86 seats in the joint Federal Assembly, where 124 are needed to win, so many FDP and Centre members or SVP dissidents would have to join them. Centre's Reto Nause said he could not vote for anyone involved in a 2024 scuffle at the Federal Palace, which involved both nominees. Koppel said he would prefer Schnegg or Ticino Council of States member Marco Chiesa as a surprise candidate.
Parliament elects Parmelin's successor on December 9.
stories.summary: Criticism of the Swiss People's Party's nomination of Thomas Aeschi and Michael Graber to succeed Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin widened over the weekend, with the Social Democrats and Greens weighing a rival candidate. Even former SVP National Councillor Roger Koppel, publisher of Weltwoche, called the pairing a serious mistake that parliament was unlikely to accept.

stories.headline: Zurich police deny using plainclothes officers as provocateurs at youth protest
more: Other media reported masked plainclothes officers, some in protective goggles and at least one carrying a baton, and said they made several arrests on the edges of the march, which was largely peaceful. Police reported 33 arrests in total, including four people referred to prosecutors for obstructing officials, and about 60 orders to leave the area.

Police spokeswoman Judith Hoedl said plainclothes deployments at potentially violent protests are routine, that such officers carry out targeted arrests of people who threaten public safety, and that they never take part in or incite violence.
stories.summary: Zurich city police rejected accusations that masked plainclothes officers provoked protesters and journalists during Friday evening's youth demonstration, part of a Europe-wide youth strike. Journalist Raimond Lueppken said on Instagram that officers deliberately provoked reporters and tried to knock phones out of their hands.

briefs.text: European Council President Antonio Costa proposed cutting 204 billion euros from the Commission's 2 trillion euro EU budget plan for 2028-2034 and adding a 3 percent digital tax on large tech firms. Germany has led calls for a smaller budget; EU leaders meet next week.
The CDU drew widespread mockery for an Instagram post portraying Chancellor Merz as a Grand Theft Auto character with 'missions' such as border turnbacks and scrapping the citizen's allowance.
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the bench after a month out with a viral infection, saying he has fully recovered.

stories.headline: Poll: half of Germans want Ukraine aid cut, and many want Merz to meet Putin
more: In the same survey of 2,329 adults, taken November 13 to 16, 49 percent said Chancellor Friedrich Merz should meet Russian President Vladimir Putin as soon as possible, even without Russian concessions; 9 percent opposed a meeting.

Merz remains deeply unpopular: 12 percent were satisfied with his work in ARD's November DeutschlandTrend, up from a record-low 10 percent in October. YouGov's November voting-intention poll puts the far-right AfD at 29 percent against 19 percent for the CDU/CSU.
stories.summary: Forty-nine percent of Germans want support for Ukraine reduced or ended, according to a YouGov poll for Welt am Sonntag: 25 percent want all aid stopped and 24 percent want it scaled back. Thirty percent want current levels kept and 9 percent want more.

stories.headline: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs at Frankfurt and Munich hubs
more: Management blamed the Middle East war, high fuel costs, nine days of strikes this year and a high cost base, and said the airline lost an average of 20 million euros a month in the first nine months of the year. The wider Lufthansa group reported a 30 percent rise in third-quarter profits.

It is not yet clear which roles are affected, when the cuts will happen, or whether they are part of an earlier plan to eliminate 4,000 jobs by 2030. The board will take employees' questions at a session on Tuesday, November 24, and is also considering further cuts to short- and medium-haul flights.
stories.summary: Lufthansa Airlines plans to cut 1,000 full-time positions at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, about 2.5 percent of its roughly 40,000 staff. Its board said previous turnaround measures were no longer enough to secure the airline's future.

briefs.text: The San Francisco Zoo raised 62 young endangered San Francisco garter snakes and released them this fall at selected sites in San Mateo County, the first successful head-starting release for a species thought to number fewer than 2,000 in the wild; more than 130 more zoo-born snakes are slated for release in 2027.

In a small study in the New England Journal of Medicine, 6 to 12 months of a new class of drug that blocks aldosterone production left almost a quarter of 14 patients with a common hormonal cause of high blood pressure with normal readings and no other medicine, with benefits lasting up to two years, Queen Mary University of London said; a larger trial is planned.

A single infusion of the CRISPR gene-editing therapy CTX310 cut triglycerides by an average of 63 percent, and up to 85 percent, after 30 days in 10 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia, with no serious treatment-related side effects, Cleveland Clinic researchers reported at the American Heart Association meeting.

stories.headline: Experimental malaria vaccine protects 13 of 15 volunteers in early trial
more: All seven volunteers who got a placebo became infected, compared with two of the 15 who were vaccinated; everyone infected was treated promptly. Volunteers were challenged 12 to 16 weeks after their last dose with a Brazilian parasite strain different from the West African strain used to make the vaccine, and the shot was reported to be safe and well tolerated.

The vaccine strain was created at Seattle Children's and developed and manufactured by Sanaria Inc. of Rockville, Maryland. The trial was sponsored by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases and run at the University of Washington School of Medicine; the findings were presented at a conference and have not yet appeared in a journal.
stories.summary: A genetically weakened whole-parasite malaria vaccine called PfSPZ-LARC2 protected 13 of 15 vaccinated adults who were deliberately exposed to malaria in a phase 1 trial, an efficacy of about 87 percent. The results were presented on November 19 at the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene annual meeting near Washington, D.C.

briefs.text: The Migration Agency's citizenship units passed 637 applicants on for possible permit-revocation checks between November 2024 and the end of 2025, under government directives; annual revocations rose from 1,371 in 2022 to 5,398 in 2025.

Prosecutors charged six final-year pupils at Sigtuna Humanistiska Laroverk boarding school over alleged abuse of younger pupils, two of them with sexual assault and aggravated assault; all deny the charges.

stories.headline: Left Party rejects red-green 'starter package' without cabinet seats
more: The package included rent reductions, a dental care reform, curbs on unreasonable deportations and state secretary posts, and Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson apologized for the 2019 January Agreement's wording aimed at sidelining the Left. Gabrielsson objected to the offer being made public in an Expressen opinion piece.

Centre Party deputy leader Rickard Nordin called it the Left's last chance to make Andersson prime minister and said his party would otherwise have to consider other options. Speaker Andreas Norlen plans a new round of consultations on November 24 or 25; if parliament rejects a prime ministerial candidate four times, an extra election must be held.
stories.summary: Sweden's Left Party on Sunday turned down an offer from the Social Democrats, Greens and Centre Party that would give it policy influence and a place in an inner circle of party leaders but no ministerial posts. Deputy leader Ida Gabrielsson replied 'Thanks, but no thanks' and said the party would not change its demand for cabinet seats.

briefs.text: ICE officers detained a Mexican father and daughter on a jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma airport before an Alaska Airlines flight; their lawyer says they were traveling to a family baptism, are seeking asylum and have no criminal record, while ICE says both overstayed visas and the daughter threw hot coffee at officers, which the lawyer disputes.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said it was entirely appropriate for Trump to call Vladimir Putin a friend in the setting of last week's summit with Xi Jinping, but declined to call Putin a friend of the United States, citing the war in Ukraine.

A Southern Natural Gas pipeline caught fire late Saturday near Ward in Sumter County, Alabama, lighting up the night sky; the operator said no one was hurt, the segment was shut down and deliveries were not affected, and the cause is under investigation.

stories.headline: Democrats reach 258 House seats, their largest majority since 1992
more: Four House races remain uncalled: one each in Minnesota and Tennessee and two in Louisiana, which go to a December runoff. Republicans will have at least 173 seats, down from their 218-214 majority under Speaker Mike Johnson.

Hakeem Jeffries is expected to be elected speaker on Jan. 3. Democrats are preparing a 100-day agenda on living costs, including votes to reverse Medicaid cuts and restore expired Affordable Care Act tax credits, along with investigations of President Trump and his family's wealth; the White House has warned against such probes. Jim Jordan will lead House Republicans in the minority.
In Georgia, Sen. Jon Ossoff won reelection over Republican Mike Collins by about 18 points, fueling 2028 speculation, although he says he has no interest in running for president.
stories.summary: Democrats have won at least 258 of the 435 House seats, a gain of 44, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, according to AP race calls. It is the party's biggest House majority since Bill Clinton's first election in 1992. Democrats also hold a 56-seat Senate majority.

stories.headline: Appeals court strikes down pregnant workers law over proxy voting
more: The case was brought by Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. The ruling directly applies in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi, but advocates warn it could threaten the law elsewhere and open challenges to other laws passed by proxy vote. The eight dissenters noted that no lawmaker raised a quorum objection when the $1.7 trillion spending bill passed.
The advocacy group A Better Balance expects the case to go to the Supreme Court. The Justice Department, which has defended the law, did not immediately comment.
stories.summary: The full 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals voted 9-8 on Friday to strike down the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, which requires employers to accommodate pregnant workers. The majority ruled Congress violated the Constitution's quorum clause when it passed the law in 2022 with most House members voting by COVID-era proxy rather than being physically present.

stories.headline: Army says it will blow up unstable explosives despite court pause
more: The Army reported in March that 68 drums of lead azide had begun recrystallizing. Residents and critics fear a plume of lead dust could reach parts of Iowa and Illinois; the Army says it will take steps to limit dispersal.

The 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals granted environmental groups an emergency pause, and a federal court suspended the plan indefinitely on Friday. On Sunday, the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club filed expert and local government declarations challenging the Army's risk assessment.
stories.summary: The U.S. Army says it plans to detonate several tons of deteriorating lead azide explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on or by Tuesday, invoking an emergency exclusion to its EPA permit even though a court has paused the plan. The Army argues a controlled blast is far safer than an uncontrolled one as temperatures drop below freezing.

stories.headline: Delta system failure delays more than 1,000 flights at start of Thanksgiving week
more: A ground delay program for Delta flights at Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson airport was later lifted, and Delta said it was using manual workarounds while it restored automation. AAA projects nearly 6 million people will fly domestically during Thanksgiving week.
stories.summary: A systemwide network problem with Delta Air Lines' baggage system forced staff to handle bags by hand on Sunday, delaying more than 1,160 Delta flights by midday, 712 of them at Atlanta, according to FlightAware. The FAA said the problem was not related to its air traffic systems.

briefs.text: Mexico's Defense Ministry said seven alleged gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the operation to capture cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro' in Guasave, Sinaloa; his alleged second-in-command and a financial operator were also detained and handed to prosecutors in Mexico City.

Trump said he wants a permanent deal with Iran that bars it from nuclear weapons; Iran said a Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran's demands, including an end to the U.S. blockade of its ports and sanctions relief, must be met before talks on the Strait of Hormuz.

The United Arab Emirates condemned an Iranian attack that Bahrain said set fire to a civilian industrial facility, the fourth attempted Iranian attack in Bahrain in about a week; no injuries were reported.

stories.headline: Russian warship hit by sea drones at Libyan naval base
more: The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, said at least four drones were intercepted and two hit the ship; no casualties were reported. The eastern government confirmed an explosion and fire, said the ship had docked for fuel and supplies under a cooperation deal with Russia, and opened a joint investigation with Moscow.
No group claimed responsibility, and neither Russia nor Ukraine commented. The rival government in western Libya said the country must not become a battleground for foreign powers.
stories.summary: Two military officials in eastern Libya said sea drones struck the Russian navy corvette Merkury at the Benghazi naval base on Sunday, severely damaging it. They said an initial investigation pointed to Ukraine, with the drones allegedly launched from a Ukrainian-run base in western Libya.

stories.headline: Poland says Russia tried twice to kill Ukrainian American rapper
more: Danish security service PET said two men linked to a banned gang have been charged with attempted murder and helping a foreign intelligence service; Denmark expelled Russia's defense attache. In Poland, a Russian citizen allegedly recruited by Russian services was detained on Aug. 7.

Russia's FSB has accused Vasiliev of supplying drones for an attack near Moscow, which he denies. Denmark is expected to seek tougher EU measures, possibly limiting Russians' free travel within the bloc, and Poland said it would support that.
stories.summary: Poland said Sunday that a plot it foiled in August targeted Albert Vasiliev, a Ukrainian American rapper known as Kyivstoner, days after Denmark said Russian intelligence planned to kill him at a concert near Copenhagen in September. Russia's embassy in Denmark called the accusations unsubstantiated.

stories.headline: Displaced Gazans protest as Israeli strikes continue despite ceasefire
more: Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,661 people have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire. Local officials said more than 500 housing units were destroyed in under a month, and the Maghazi mayor accused Israel of a policy of creeping displacement. Israel did not comment in the report.

Nearly two-thirds of Gaza is now under Israeli military control or access restrictions, after Israeli forces took more territory instead of pulling back further as expected under the U.S.-brokered plan.
stories.summary: Hundreds of displaced Palestinians protested in Deir el-Balah against intensifying Israeli air strikes and demolitions of homes near the so-called Yellow Line, Al Jazeera reported. At least four Palestinians were killed Saturday, including three when a drone hit a van delivering food aid in Gaza City.

lead.headline: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran says it struck U.S. radar in Bahrain
more: Al Jazeera's Tehran correspondent, citing Iranian military statements, said about 25 shipping incidents had been reported over the past week. Iran insists ships coordinate with its authorities and use lanes it sets. Before the war, the strait carried nearly a fifth of the world's crude oil supply; the U.S. has blockaded Iranian ports and escorts tankers.
The Revolutionary Guards also said they shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone over the strait and an MQ-1 over Qeshm Island; there was no immediate U.S. comment. Bahrain said no one was injured in the fire.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran's seven conditions, including an end to the war and the lifting of sanctions and the naval blockade, must be met for the strait to reopen, and ruled out sending its enriched uranium abroad. President Trump said Tehran wants a deal but not one he can accept. The U.S. Treasury on Friday sanctioned four Iranians it accused of handling revenue from illicit oil sales.
lead.summary: Two oil tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman's Khasab on Saturday, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said, with no casualties reported. Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted area after ignoring warnings. Iran's Revolutionary Guards also said they attacked U.S. air defense radar at two air bases in Bahrain, where authorities reported a fire at an industrial facility. Efforts to end the nine-month war remain stalled.

briefs.text: MeteoSwiss and Alertswiss warned of heavy rain and snow, with 40 to 60 centimeters of fresh snow possible locally above 1,500 meters.
About 10,000 people joined an authorized demonstration in Lausanne; afterward a smaller group attacked police with pyrotechnics.
About 2,000 media workers protested job cuts in Bern.
The Federal Supreme Court rejected appeals against the e-ID vote, ruling that late-disclosed in-kind campaign contributions of about 163,000 francs were not enough to annul the result.
A 17-year-old passenger was killed when a car driven by an 18-year-old crashed in Sonvico, Ticino, shortly before midnight.

stories.headline: SVP picks Aeschi and Graber to succeed Parmelin
more: The caucus needed 13 rounds of secret ballots to choose between eight hopefuls. Those left off the ticket included Geneva National Councillor and party vice president Celine Amaudruz and former party president Marco Chiesa of Ticino.

The Greens called the ticket a provocation and said their group would not hold hearings with the two men. The women's alliance Alliance F criticized the exclusion of Amaudruz, and the choice means the French-speaking region is expected to lose the seat Parmelin held.
stories.summary: The Swiss People's Party (SVP) parliamentary group nominated its caucus leader Thomas Aeschi of Zug and Michael Graber of Upper Valais as candidates to replace Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin, who steps down at the end of the year. Parliament elects his successor on December 9.

stories.headline: Polls point to tight race on arms exports a week before national vote
more: The SRG SSR poll by gfs.bern put the arms-export revision at 49 percent yes, as did a Tamedia/20 Minuten survey; YouGov found 42 percent yes, 37 percent no and about one in five undecided. The VAT increase drew 51 to 57 percent opposition across the three polls.

Support for the Centre party's initiative on taxing married couples has slipped: SRG SSR and Tamedia now show majorities against it, while YouGov had 45 percent yes and 42 percent no. The fireworks initiative polled between 59 and 63 percent yes.
stories.summary: Swiss voters decide four federal proposals on November 29. Recent polls show a revision of the War Materiel Act too close to call, a VAT increase to fund the 13th OASI pension payment trailing, and an initiative to restrict fireworks comfortably ahead.

stories.headline: IG Metall stages first 24-hour warning strike in eight years
more: About 3.7 million employees are covered by the industry's collective agreement. Employers said the strikes cause significant damage in a tense economy; the union says further action is expected next week.

Separately, Volkswagen presented cost-cutting demands for talks covering about 120,000 workers at its core brand, including pay freezes in 2027 and 2028 and unpaid hours beyond the 35-hour week when needed. IG Metall called the list a catalogue of horrors.
stories.summary: Germany's largest union, IG Metall, called metal and electrical workers out on a 24-hour warning strike on Friday after employers rejected its pay demands in a third round of talks. Walkouts hit shipyards in the north, suppliers in Baden-Wuerttemberg and BMW and Audi plants in Bavaria.

stories.headline: Young Germans march again against conscription and cuts
more: About 5,000 people registered for a separate pupils' demonstration at the Brandenburg Gate, and about 400 marched against conscription in Frankfurt, where police deployed about 2,000 officers after rioting at protests three weeks earlier, dpa reported.
Education Minister Karin Prien said young people have a right to be heard. A co-organizer of Gen Z Takes Charge said the protests would continue regardless of any talks.
stories.summary: Thousands of young people demonstrated in Berlin on Friday in the latest Gen Z protests, with smaller marches in Frankfurt, Cologne, Bremen and Hamburg, part of a Europe-wide day of action. Organizers demanded more money for schools, mental-health support and affordable housing and rejected military conscription.

stories.headline: Qatar pledges 15 billion euros more investment during emir's Berlin visit
more: The two governments also agreed to work together on protection against cyberattacks, and Germany said it was interested in defense-industry partnerships. Talks covered efforts to end the war involving Iran and to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; President Frank-Walter Steinmeier was invited to the Doha Forum on December 5-6.
stories.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Qatar pledged an additional 15 billion euros of investment in Germany during talks with Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Berlin on Friday. The money is to support cooperation in artificial intelligence, computer chips and aviation.

briefs.text: Bangladesh and India declared national bans in September on paraquat, a highly toxic weedkiller, joining more than 70 countries that prohibit it; the World Health Organization said on November 12 the bans will save thousands of lives and protect farm workers' health.

Five more major methane leaks flagged by the UN Environment Programme's satellite alert system have been fixed since June, in Canada, Iraq, Kazakhstan and Mexico, preventing about 125,000 tonnes of the potent greenhouse gas, UNEP said; the total now stands at 46 sources in 13 countries.

The Global Fund for Coral Reefs announced more than $30 million in new investments and donor money at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, to protect and restore reefs and support coastal communities in 22 developing countries.

stories.headline: Scientists read a whale's whole genome from breath caught by a drone
more: The study, published in Molecular Ecology Resources, used 58 breath samples from 26 North Pacific humpbacks in the Kitimat Fjord System in Gitga'at First Nation territory in northern British Columbia. About 84 percent of the DNA came from the whales themselves, and genomes from breath matched those from biopsies of the same animals.

Before the work, only one whole genome from a North Pacific humpback was publicly available. More than a third of the samples were gathered with drones flown straight from land, and the team found three previously undescribed mitochondrial DNA variants.

sources.name: University of St Andrews via EurekAlert!

stories.summary: Researchers have sequenced a complete humpback whale genome using only the spray from a whale's exhaled breath, collected by a small drone, the University of St Andrews said on November 17. The team called it a world first, showing that detailed genetic studies of whales are possible without darts, biopsies or close approaches by boat.

briefs.text: Unemployment fell to 7.7 percent in October from 8.9 percent a year earlier, according to Statistics Sweden figures.
Hackers breached the booking system of the Universeum science center, exposing data on about 280,000 visitors; police are also investigating suspected theft of customer data from taxi firm Cabonline.
Sweden summoned the Russian ambassador over attacks in Ukraine, including one near the Swedish embassy.

EU Affairs Minister Jessica Rosencrantz said a revised EU long-term budget proposal, which includes a 3 percent tax on big digital companies, is still too large; Sweden is among the frugal states pushing for a smaller budget.

stories.headline: Red-green talks end in deadlock as Speaker summons party leaders
more: Speaker Andreas Norlen will meet party leaders one by one on Tuesday and brief the press afterward. A vote on a prime minister could come late next week or early the following week; Norlen has said it must be clear well before Christmas whether Sweden gets a new government or a snap election, which is triggered if four votes fail.
stories.summary: Talks among the Social Democrats, Left Party, Centre Party and Greens on forming a government broke up on Friday without agreement after the leaders spent three days at an undisclosed location. The Left and Centre parties blamed each other, with the main sticking point the Left's demand for cabinet posts, which the Centre rejects.

stories.headline: Swedish police to open station in Iraq to pursue fleeing gang members
more: Lundh told Swedish Radio's Ekot that police have built up cooperation with the countries where Swedish gang leaders have fled and are now stepping it up.
stories.summary: National Police Commissioner Petra Lundh said police will open a pilot station in Iraq early next year to target gang criminals who have fled Sweden. Four more overseas stations are planned over the next two years, possibly including North Africa.

briefs.text: Federal and local agents dismantled what the DEA called the first nitazene synthesis lab found in the U.S., in the basement of a Baton Rouge, Louisiana, home; its reactor held etonitazene, a synthetic opioid far stronger than fentanyl.
Democratic Reps. Yassamin Ansari and Ro Khanna urged Congress to bar funding for offensive operations against Iran in the spending bill due by Dec. 11 to avoid a government shutdown.

stories.headline: FBI investigating apparent hack of national crime database
more: CNN first reported the incident. The FBI declined to comment. President Trump told Fox News officials had just learned of it and called it "not good."

It follows a string of digital outages in government and business that administration officials have blamed on routine upgrades rather than cyberattacks; there was no immediate sign the incidents are linked. The FBI has been hacked before, including a breach of its job portal in September.
stories.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center, the database police across the country use to check fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property, a person familiar with the matter told the AP on Saturday. The scope of the breach was not immediately clear.

stories.headline: Trump tells federal contractors to clear congressional requests with White House
more: The White House says the order protects executive privilege from congressional overreach. It comes before Democrats take control of Congress in January, and they have named government contracts, including Pentagon money going to companies linked to Trump's family, a top oversight target.
Presidents of both parties have used executive privilege to resist congressional inquiries, which often leads to long legal fights; the protection is not absolute.
stories.summary: President Trump ordered federal contractors and subcontractors late Friday to consult the administration about inquiries from Congress and to withhold communications the White House considers privileged. Companies that do not comply could lose their contracts and be barred from future federal work.

stories.headline: Trump says he will work with Democrats on 10% credit card rate cap
more: Banks have warned a cap would lead them to cancel cards for riskier borrowers or cut rewards, and the Republican-led Congress did little with the idea. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, and Republican Sen. Josh Hawley have both backed caps.
Researchers estimate a 10% cap would save Americans about $100 billion a year in interest. No legislation has been scheduled.
stories.summary: President Trump said Saturday he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, a 2024 campaign promise he has not delivered. The median card rate is about 22.2%, according to a New York Fed survey.

stories.headline: Witness says Texas inmate cried out in pain during execution
more: A prison spokesperson said procedures were followed, there would be no further inquiry, and there were reasons to suspect Dennes was exaggerating. A medical toxicologist said he could not explain the leg pain Dennes described. It was Texas's ninth execution this year, and lethal injections have drawn new scrutiny after a failed execution in Tennessee in September.
stories.summary: Texas executed 70-year-old Reinaldo Dennes by lethal injection on Thursday after staff failed to place IV lines in his arms and hands and instead used his neck and foot. His spiritual adviser said Dennes repeatedly cried out in pain and called the execution torture; the state says it went as planned.

Countries meeting under a U.N. weapons convention in Geneva agreed to work on a possible accord on lethal autonomous weapons over the next two years; nearly 100 nations wanted binding rules sooner, but the U.S., Russia and Israel opposed.
At least 11 people died and more than 180 were hospitalized after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India's Manipur state; the chief minister ordered an investigation.

Members of India's opposition Youth Congress protested outside Meta offices in three cities, accusing the company of restricting opposition leaders' Instagram accounts on the ruling BJP's orders; Meta has not publicly responded.

stories.headline: Mexico captures cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off deadly violence
more: Gunmen set up at least 10 roadblocks with burning vehicles and torched businesses while military helicopters and drones fired on locations around the city. Troops did not get him out until about 4 a.m. Saturday; he was flown to Mexico City to face prosecutors.

The U.S. had offered a $5 million reward on drug trafficking and weapons charges, and Mexico said U.S. intelligence helped. Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said troops would remain in Sinaloa, where cartel factions are fighting for control.
stories.summary: Mexican forces detained Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro" and one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, in Guasave, Sinaloa, after a firefight that began Friday evening. At least 11 people were killed, including four soldiers and seven alleged gunmen, authorities said.

stories.headline: COP31 president says climate deal is within reach
more: Kurum said the revised text addressed concerns over fossil fuels and adaptation finance for developing countries. An earlier draft had dropped language on ending fossil fuel use and a proposed $120 billion adaptation target, drawing sharp criticism; observers said Saudi Arabia and other oil producers opposed fossil fuel language.
The United States is not taking part for a second year. The next summit is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in November 2027.
stories.summary: COP31 president Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary in Antalya, Turkey, that negotiators had a text all parties could accept, after the summit ran more than a day past its Friday deadline. Delegations were to approve it at a session Sunday morning.

stories.headline: Drones hit Russia-bound cargo ship in Gulf of Finland
more: No one has claimed the attack. Finland sent Border Guard units, restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern gulf and prepared for possible environmental cleanup. Earlier this month, Ukraine took credit for a strike on a Russian warship in the gulf, prompting Helsinki to raise concerns with Kyiv.
stories.summary: Two drones struck a cargo ship bound for Russia's Kaliningrad exclave in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday morning, a senior Russian official said. Finland's Border Guard said the ship was on fire, and Russian officials said the crew was being evacuated.

stories.headline: Russian missiles kill two in Zelenskyy's hometown
more: About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools were damaged. Russian-installed authorities said a Ukrainian attack killed six people in occupied Luhansk. asl.hook: Think of working with a hammer: one fist pounds on the other.
steps: Make fists (the S handshape) with both hands.
Turn both palms to face down.
Hold your non-dominant fist still in front of you.
Tap the wrist or side of it with your dominant fist a few times.
asl.tip: Many signers use a handshape between an A and an S, especially on the dominant hand; that is fine. For a job, the sign JOB is more common.

onThisDay.text: Jean-Francois Pilatre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes made the first free flight carrying people, in a hot-air balloon built by the Montgolfier brothers. They lifted off from the garden of the Chateau de la Muette in Paris in front of the king, rose to about 3,000 feet and drifted about 9 kilometers in some 25 minutes before landing at the Butte-aux-Cailles. Two months earlier, a sheep, a duck and a rooster had made a test flight at Versailles.
onThisDay.title: First Balloon Flight

swedish.example: Ursäkta, vad är klockan? – Den är halv tre.
swedish.exampleMeaning: Excuse me, what time is it? – It's half past two.
swedish.note: Watch out with halv: halv tre means half way to three, so 2:30, not 3:30. The answer always starts with Den är (It is).

swissGerman.example: Ich mach grad Kafi. Wottsch au eine?
swissGerman.exampleMeaning: I'm just making coffee. Do you want one too?
swissGerman.note: Kafi is the everyday Swiss word for coffee, stressed on the first syllable. Wottsch is the Zurich form of willst du; to a group or politely you would say Wänd Sie en Kafi?

lead.headline: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% as AI sell-off pushes market into correction
more: Nvidia fell 13.8%, and is down more than 25% since the scandal that led co-founder Jensen Huang to resign as chief executive on Nov. 12. AMD lost 13.3%, Micron 13.9% and Broadcom 12.1%; the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 10.7%. Anthropic shares dropped 9.1% to $88.30, still above their $83 IPO price.
The S&P 500 posted its worst week since April 2025. Its seven-day losing streak was the longest since early 2020. Most stocks outside tech rose. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.91%.

CBS News also pointed to proposed limits on data center construction expected after the midterm elections, and to a Dec. 11 government funding deadline. A Baird strategist said the idea that AI spending can keep propping up the market is ending, but that he does not think the bull market that began in October 2022 is over.
lead.summary: U.S. stocks suffered one of their worst days in years on Friday as a sell-off in artificial intelligence and chip stocks deepened. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39, putting it more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record and in a correction, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3% and turned negative for the year. The Dow lost 949.73 points, or 1.9%. Investors are questioning whether heavy AI spending will pay off, amid fallout from the Nvidia leadership scandal, tighter chip export rules, expected Fed rate increases and tensions with Iran.

briefs.text: Young Socialists (Jusos) planned protests on Friday in Zurich, Basel, Bern, Lausanne and other cities as part of a Europe-wide movement against militarization and austerity; organizers said no riots were planned.
The French-speaking cantons and Ticino want to strengthen German teaching from primary school onward, calling skills in a national language essential for national cohesion.

stories.headline: Parts of Swiss Alps put on high avalanche alert
more: The level 4 zones include Bex-Villars, the Wildhorn area, western and northern Lower Valais and the Martigny-Verbier area, where the main risk is avalanches set off by the weight of the snow itself, possibly reaching lower elevations. Parts of eastern Switzerland are at level 3, where a single person on a steep slope can trigger a slide.

Up to 50 centimeters of fresh snow could fall on northern slopes above 1,800 meters, and the Bernese Oberland could get up to 30 centimeters more by Sunday along with gale-force winds. About 20 people die in avalanches in Switzerland in an average year.
stories.summary: The Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research (SLF) raised the avalanche danger to level 4, the second-highest on its scale, for parts of Vaud, Valais and Bern on Friday. Heavy snowfall is forecast to continue through Sunday.

stories.headline: Left launches initiative to cut health insurance premiums
more: Backers say 90 percent of the population would benefit. They must now collect enough signatures to force a nationwide vote.
stories.summary: The Social Democrats, the Greens and trade unions announced a popular initiative on Thursday that would make insurers waive two months of premiums a year for each adult and six months for each child. The plan would cost about 8 billion francs a year, funded by a higher direct federal tax on individual income and business profits.

stories.headline: Zurich University Hospital pays first compensation in heart surgery scandal
more: The hospital says all cases so far were settled out of court and several claims are still pending. A report in May found 68 to 74 more deaths than statistically expected among about 4,500 heart operations under former department head Francesco Maisano.
Zurich prosecutors are investigating three cases on suspicion of negligent homicide, negligent serious bodily harm and document forgery.
stories.summary: The University Hospital of Zurich (USZ) has paid compensation in 14 cases to patients or surviving relatives affected by failings in its cardiac surgery department. It has received 20 claims in total, and the payments so far add up to a low six-figure sum in francs.

briefs.text: Leaked Deutsche Bank documents point to a suspected Russian money-laundering network that moved at least 1.7 billion euros through Hungary's MKB bank between 2017 and 2020, according to Hungarian outlet Direkt36; Deutsche Bank ended its relationship with MKB.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves overhaul of custody and child support rules
more: The Justice Ministry calls the custody bill the biggest reform of child law since 1998. It defines domestic violence to include physical, sexual, psychological and economic abuse and would let the parent caring for a child make routine decisions alone. It is expected to take effect in the second half of 2027 at the earliest.

From 2029, single parents with taxable income above 40,000 euros a year, plus 10,000 euros for each additional child, would lose entitlement to advance maintenance. Parents who owe support and refuse to disclose their finances could face fines or a driving ban. Both bills still need Bundestag approval.
stories.summary: The federal cabinet approved two draft bills that would let courts bar contact with a parent who is violent toward the other parent and give teenagers aged 14 and over a greater say in custody arrangements. A second bill would tighten state advance maintenance payments for single parents.

stories.headline: Conservatives make new push to tighten citizenship rules
more: The proposal from Guenter Krings and Alexander Throm would reverse much of the 2024 reform. The coalition partner SPD has so far blocked such changes, but Bild reported that its leadership is reviewing the proposal, which may be offered in exchange for stronger residency rights for foreigners in work or training. Party leaders are expected to discuss it next week.
stories.summary: CDU/CSU lawmakers proposed raising the residency requirement for naturalization back to eight years from five, allowing dual citizenship only in exceptional cases and requiring B2-level German. The plan would also bar applicants who receive social assistance.

stories.headline: Electricity tax cut for all households to return in 2027
more: Funding is secured only through the end of 2027 from the renewable-energy surcharge account; the coalition says it intends the cut to be permanent but must find financing in the 2028 budget. Comparison site Verivox estimates a three-person household using 4,000 kilowatt-hours would save about 7.75 euros a month. The Bundestag is due to vote on the 2027 budget on November 27.
stories.summary: Coalition leaders agreed after more than eight hours of budget talks to cut the electricity tax for all households and businesses from 2.05 cents to 0.1 cents per kilowatt-hour, the EU minimum, starting January 1. The cut will cost about 5.4 billion euros a year.

briefs.text: Native oysters have bred naturally in Scotland's Dornoch Firth for the first time in more than a century, Heriot-Watt University said, after a restoration project that has released over 140,000 juvenile oysters since 2017 found young spat growing on the seabed.

Britain's Judicial Committee of the Privy Council ruled unanimously on November 10 that Trinidad and Tobago's laws criminalizing consensual sex between adults of the same sex are unconstitutional, in a case brought by activist Jason Jones.

stories.headline: Eritrea eliminates trachoma as a public health problem
more: Eritrea surveyed all 58 of its sub-zobas between 2006 and 2020 and applied WHO's SAFE strategy of eyelid surgery, antibiotics, facial cleanliness and better water and sanitation, using azithromycin donated by Pfizer through the International Trachoma Initiative. It is the 66th country to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease.

Worldwide, the number of people needing trachoma interventions fell from about 1.5 billion in 2002 to below 100 million by November 2025, a drop of about 94 percent. WHO says 92 million people still lived in endemic areas as of March 2026, and the disease remains a public health problem in parts of 29 countries.
stories.summary: The World Health Organization said on November 16 that it has validated Eritrea's elimination of trachoma, the world's leading infectious cause of blindness, as a public health problem. Eritrea is the 34th country worldwide and the 11th in WHO's African Region to reach the milestone. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said two decades of effort had consigned the disease to history in the country.

briefs.text: Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson costed the Social Democrats' policy offers to the Centre Party at 175 billion kronor; Centre leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist said the package would be unsustainable in full and must be negotiated.
Six pupils at the Sigtunaskolan Humanistiska Laroverket boarding school were charged with bullying and assaulting younger students, two of them with serious sexual assault; all deny wrongdoing.
Forsmark 1 and 3 nuclear reactors were due back online after maintenance and a cable fault, easing power supply; Vattenfall said Ringhals 3 and 4 will not restart until early December.
More than nine in ten women feel safe with Swedish maternity care, a survey by the association of local authorities and regions found, though many report too little follow-up after birth.

stories.headline: Snow warning issued for Stockholm and Uppsala
more: The warning covers an area from Nynashamn and Sodertalje in the south to Tierp in the north. Along the northern Uppland coast most of the precipitation is expected to fall as rain.
stories.summary: The weather agency SMHI issued a yellow warning for 5 to 15 centimeters of fresh snow in the Stockholm and Uppsala area from Friday evening to Saturday evening. It warned of longer travel times and possible public transport delays and cancellations.

stories.headline: Trial opens for teenager accused of planning IS-inspired school attack
more: He was arrested at 18, the day after the Easter holidays. Prosecutors say he planned to use a kitchen knife; his defense lawyer argues the risk he would have carried out an attack was small and that he had no real links to IS.
stories.summary: A 19-year-old went on trial charged with preparing a terrorist offense after prosecutors said he planned to kill 15 people at his upper secondary school in Halmstad. He denies the charge, saying he changed his mind at the last minute, but admits taking part in a terrorist organization and publicly inciting terrorism.

briefs.text: The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday for a bipartisan bill to speed up approvals for power plants and transmission lines. The bill would also make large AI data centers pay more toward grid upgrades. It now goes to the House.
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close Rikers Island by 2032, five years later than the previous deadline. Four smaller borough jails would replace it.

A federal appeals court blocked the Army from detonating several tons of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa over health concerns. Separately, a second federal judge halted construction of Trump's planned memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery.
Trump said Nvidia should give Jensen Huang a second chance, but Nvidia's board chair said directors do not plan to reinstate him.

stories.headline: U.S. and Israel weigh new strikes on Iran, sources say
more: Sources said an offensive could begin within two to four days if ordered. The U.S. has tens of thousands of troops and two carrier strike groups in the region.

Indirect talks have not produced a ceasefire to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and tit-for-tat strikes continue nine months into the war. Iran's Foreign Ministry compared U.S. allegations about Iranian weapons to the case made before the 2003 invasion of Iraq.
stories.summary: Israel and the United States are considering a new military assault on Iran in the near term, CBS News reported, citing unnamed sources. Israel is concerned that Iran is rebuilding ballistic missile production and moving sites underground. President Trump said he was not rushing into any decision.

stories.headline: Man convicted of starting deadly Palisades Fire
more: Prosecutors said a fire he started on Jan. 1, 2025, smoldered underground and flared up on Jan. 7, becoming one of the most destructive wildfires in California history. They relied on cellphone data, camera images and his texts.
The defense argued the scene had been open to the public for days and that fireworks may have caused the fire.
stories.summary: A federal jury in a retrial on Friday convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of arson and destroying property by fire in connection with the January 2025 Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people. The first trial ended in a mistrial in June.

stories.headline: String of U.S. outages raises cybersecurity concerns
more: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the outages likely came from organizations using AI to fix security flaws and run maintenance updates. Experts quoted by Al Jazeera said the administration is not taking AI-driven threats seriously, noting that the cybersecurity agency CISA lost more than a third of its staff in 2025 cuts.
stories.summary: A series of recent outages hit major banks, Microsoft, Apple and Workday, along with a national aviation ground stop and an NSA internal network. President Trump told the public to relax, calling them individual events, and the White House fired the U.S. cybersecurity chief on Thursday.

briefs.text: Denmark is expelling Russia's defense attache after its intelligence service said Russian agents planned to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a Copenhagen-area concert in September. Russia's embassy said Denmark had shown no evidence.
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh after it struck Hodeidah port and Sanaa. The Houthis have threatened Saudi ports and power plants.
The European-Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo is about to go into orbit around Mercury, eight years after launch. It will be only the second spacecraft to orbit the planet.

stories.headline: Poland calls Russian missiles in its territory an intentional provocation
more: Possible impact sites were reported near Nowy Lipowiec, about 60 km from the Ukrainian border, and around Bilgoraj County. No casualties were reported. Poland said it would ask NATO for more help securing the alliance's eastern flank, and Rutte was due in Warsaw on Saturday.
Tusk said Poland must have a say in decisions about Ukraine's future. Russian strikes on Ukraine overnight included an attack on a railway station in the west of the country.
stories.summary: Poland said two missiles and a drone that came down in its eastern regions overnight were probably Russian. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation by Moscow. The objects came down during a military exercise involving the Coalition of the Willing, a group of European countries preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the incident clearly dangerous.

stories.headline: COP31 climate talks go into overtime over fossil fuels
more: The European Union warned the summit risked becoming a fossil summit, and Panama threatened to walk out. The new text also dropped a $120 billion target for helping poorer countries adapt.
A third draft was expected Saturday. COP31 president Murat Kurum said negotiators were close to the finish line but not there yet. The United States is absent for a second year.
stories.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye, ran past its Friday deadline without a deal. Nearly 200 countries remain split over fossil fuels. A revised draft dropped all mention of them after objections from Saudi Arabia and other oil and gas producers.

stories.headline: UK and EU agree closer trade, carbon and youth mobility ties
more: No documents were signed, and each side still has to complete legal procedures. Tuition fees for EU students and British access to EU 'Made in Europe' rules remain unresolved.
stories.summary: At a summit in Brussels on Friday, Britain and the European Union agreed to ease food and farm checks, link their carbon trading systems, and let up to 100,000 young people from each side live and work in the other's territory. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the package could add 0.5% to UK economic output.

stories.headline: Estonia to close road border with Russia from December
more: Estonia's foreign minister said the closure would limit recruitment, sabotage and sanctions evasion. Rail freight will continue under strict checks. Finland has kept its Russian crossings closed since 2023.
stories.summary: Estonia's government approved a six-month closure of all road crossings with Russia starting Dec. 1. It accused Moscow of an attempted arson attack on a drone maker, which the Kremlin denies. Russia's Foreign Ministry said the move amounted to a new Iron Curtain and promised a response.
